title.narrative: Technical Collaboration on Area-based Planning in Libya

description.narrative: Following the recent Storm Daniels flooding and cases of groundwater flooding in Zliten, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has a developed a comprehensive response and resilience strategy to support affected populations through immediate response, medium-term recovery, and long-term resilience building. UN-Habitat has established a very good relationship with the Benghazi and Derna Fund, and provided technical support for them to be able to monitor reconstruction activities in Derna, that is including the development of an online portal, which reflects on the damage assessment, of building/housing, UN-Habitat has also provided inputs and review of two sections of the Damage Assessment done by the EB, UN and the EU, however the housing damage assessment was not elaborate, hence the need for house-hold technical assessment is required. As the response is largely urban and impact urban systems, IOM has engaged a Settlements Approach framework to the response. With this consideration, and in the wider consideration of the Secretary-General's Agenda on Internal Displacement, a partnership with the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) reaffirms the two agencies’ commitments to an integrated and effective response. This partnership offers the opportunity for heightened collaboration and is aligned with both organisation’s institutional plans. This partnership leverages the strengths and expertise of both IOM and UN-Habitat, ensuring comprehensive and integrated strategies for sustainable urban environments. This enhanced synergy encompasses a range of activities from urban planning and management to data collection, analysis, and field-based displacement, housing reconstruction and urban planning strategies, tools and operations.
